attack_steps: An approved embedding attempt leaves a live Failed(auth_error) task.
The operator repairs credentials and invokes batch retry.
Embedding reconciliation ignores allow_auth_revive=false and resets the task to Pending.
The revived task passes filtering and its text is sent to the adapter in the same pass.
assumptions: Secret holds and budget checks pass.
attack_path_facts.context: Command-scoped task authorization failure in the normal embedding recovery workflow.
attack_path_facts.exposure: A local CLI recovery path reaches a configured outbound adapter call; KCS has no inbound listener.
attack_path_facts.identity: A lower-trust remote provider can create the AuthError response state; the trusted operator supplies the later recovery command.
attack_path_facts.attacker_control: The remote provider controls the failure response; a content contributor may control the already-approved chunk text, but neither controls the later operator command.
attack_path_facts.auth_scope: internal-only: only AuthError revival under batch retry is bypassed; initial adapter consent is not bypassed.
attack_path_facts.impact_surface: network: previously approved content can be resent and bounded online cost incurred contrary to the selected recovery contract
attack_path_facts.target_reach: Live AuthError embedding tasks in the selected scope.
counterevidence: The operator requested retry work generally.
Content was already approved for the same adapter.
No monetary-cap or secret-hold bypass occurs.
blindspots: Validation used the adapter seam rather than a real provider, although the real pre-adapter request path was reached.
controls: The outer retry path sets allow_auth_revive=false.
Adapter approval, secret holds, and the budget gate still execute.
attack_path_facts.rationale: A realistic lower-trust provider-response path exists and the revival/send transition is deterministic once ordinary recovery preconditions hold. The wrong command reaches a real send, but existing consent, secret, and budget controls bound impact. Medium impact plus high likelihood maps mechanically to medium.
